es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo que nadie que haya nacido jamás es más grande que Juan. Pero aun la persona menos importante en el reino de Dios es más grande que él».

sw.L: Nawaambia, miongoni mwa waliozaliwa na wanawake hakuna aliye mkuu kuliko Yohana; lakini aliye mdogo katika ufalme wa Mungu ni mkuu kuliko yeye."
sw.B: Nawaambia, kati ya wote waliozaliwa na wanawake, hakuna aliye mkuu kuliko Yohana. Hata hivyo, aliye mdogo kabisa katika ufalme wa Mungu ni mkuu kuliko yeye."
sw.R: Nawaambia, hakuna mtu aliyewahi kuzaliwa aliye mkuu kuliko Yohana. Lakini hata mtu asiye muhimu kabisa katika ufalme wa Mungu ni mkuu kuliko yeye."

decisions.choice: among those born of women: among all human beings
alternatives: among the sons of mothers only
decisions.reason: The phrase is a Hebrew way of saying all people (Job 14:1).

decisions.choice: the least: the one of lowest rank
alternatives: the lesser one, meaning Jesus, who came after John
decisions.reason: The word is a comparative, "lesser", which here has the force of "least". Some readers in the early church took it to mean Jesus, younger than John and seen as lesser. But the contrast is between all who have lived and anyone in the kingdom of God.

decisions.choice: greater than John: not in character, but in what God has given
alternatives: John is shut out of the kingdom
decisions.reason: John stands at the turning point, the last and greatest of those who announced what was coming (16:16). To share in the kingdom that has now come with Jesus is a greater gift than even John's great task.

decisions.choice: no one who has ever been born
decisions.reason: Readable says what the idiom means.

decisions.choice: the quotation closes here and opens again in 7:31
decisions.reason: 7:29-30 are the narrator's words, as the decision on 7:29 explains.

decisions.choice: el reino de Dios, at every level
decisions.reason: The book-wide term, the same phrase at every level, as the English has "the kingdom of God".

decisions.choice: ufalme wa Mungu, at every level
decisions.reason: The book-wide term, the same phrase at every level, as the English has "the kingdom of God".

source.text: καὶ πᾶς ὁ λαὸς ἀκούσας καὶ οἱ τελῶναι ἐδικαίωσαν τὸν θεόν, βαπτισθέντες τὸ βάπτισμα Ἰωάννου·

records.literal_gloss: And all the people having heard and the tax collectors declared righteous the God, having been baptized [with] the baptism of John;

en.L: And all the people who heard, even the tax collectors, justified God, having been baptized with the baptism of John;
en.B: All the people who heard this, even the tax collectors, agreed that God was in the right, because they had been baptized with John's baptism.
en.R: All the people who heard Jesus say this agreed that God's way was right. Even the tax collectors agreed. They were the ones who had let John baptize them.

es.L: Y todo el pueblo, al oír[lo], y aun los publicanos, declararon justo a Dios, habiendo sido bautizados con el bautismo de Juan;
es.B: Todo el pueblo que lo oyó, incluso los cobradores de impuestos, reconoció que Dios tenía razón, porque habían sido bautizados con el bautismo de Juan.
es.R: Toda la gente que oyó a Jesús decir esto estuvo de acuerdo en que el camino de Dios era el correcto. Hasta los cobradores de impuestos estuvieron de acuerdo. Ellos eran los que se habían dejado bautizar por Juan.

sw.L: Na watu wote waliposikia, hata watoza ushuru, walimkiri Mungu kuwa mwenye haki, wakiwa wamebatizwa kwa ubatizo wa Yohana;
sw.B: Watu wote waliosikia maneno haya, hata watoza ushuru, walikubali kwamba Mungu yuko sahihi, kwa kuwa walikuwa wamebatizwa kwa ubatizo wa Yohana.
sw.R: Watu wote waliomsikia Yesu akisema hivyo walikubali kwamba njia ya Mungu ni sahihi. Hata watoza ushuru walikubali. Wao ndio waliokuwa wamekubali kubatizwa na Yohana.

decisions.choice: 7:29-30 are the narrator's comment, not part of Jesus's speech
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT does not use quotation marks, but it ends Jesus's words with a full stop at 7:28 and starts a new paragraph at 7:31, where Jesus asks another question. 7:29-30 tell, in the past tense, how two groups had responded to John, which is how Luke the narrator speaks (compare 3:10-14 and 20:4-7). Some read the verses as Jesus's own words; the meaning would not change.

decisions.choice: justified God: declared that God was right
decisions.reason: The verb means to declare someone in the right. The people acknowledged that God's way, shown in John's call to repent, was right. The same verb returns in 7:35.

decisions.choice: who heard: who heard Jesus's words about John
decisions.reason: The verb has no object. Jesus has just spoken about John to the crowds (7:24), and the people who had accepted John's baptism agreed.

decisions.choice: tax collectors: Jews who collected taxes for Rome or its rulers, and were despised
decisions.reason: As in 3:12 and 5:27-30, these were people others looked down on. They had come to John to be baptized (3:12).

decisions.choice: agreed that God was in the right (B); agreed that God's way was right (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "justifying" God means, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: heard Jesus say this
decisions.reason: Readable says what they heard, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: publicanos (L); cobradores de impuestos (B, R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice: Literal keeps the traditional word, Balanced and Readable say what these men did (meaning decision m4). The same in verse 34.

decisions.choice: declararon justo a Dios
decisions.reason: "Declared God right" (meaning decision m2). "Justificar" in Spanish now usually means to excuse, which would point the wrong way.

decisions.choice: walimkiri Mungu kuwa mwenye haki (L); walikubali kwamba Mungu yuko sahihi (B, R)
decisions.reason: They declared that God was right (meaning decision m2). "Kuhesabiwa haki" is the phrase for being made righteous before God, which would point the wrong way when said of God; Literal says they acknowledged him to be just.

decisions.choice: watoza ushuru
decisions.reason: The book-wide word for the tax collectors (meaning decision m4), the same at every level. The same in verse 34.

source.text: οἱ δὲ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ οἱ νομικοὶ τὴν βουλὴν τοῦ θεοῦ ἠθέτησαν εἰς ἑαυτούς, μὴ βαπτισθέντες ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: The but Pharisees and the lawyers the purpose of the God rejected for themselves, not having been baptized by him.

en.L: But the Pharisees and the experts in the law set aside the purpose of God for themselves, not having been baptized by him.
en.B: But the Pharisees and the experts in the law refused what God intended for them, since they had not let John baptize them.
en.R: But the Pharisees and the experts in God's law turned away from what God wanted to do for them. They would not let John baptize them.

es.L: Pero los fariseos y los expertos en la ley rechazaron para sí mismos el propósito de Dios, no habiendo sido bautizados por él.
es.B: Pero los fariseos y los expertos en la ley rechazaron lo que Dios quería para ellos, pues no se habían dejado bautizar por Juan.
es.R: Pero los fariseos y los expertos en la ley de Dios se apartaron de lo que Dios quería hacer por ellos. No quisieron que Juan los bautizara.

sw.L: Lakini Mafarisayo na wataalamu wa sheria walilikataa kusudi la Mungu kwa ajili yao wenyewe, kwa kuwa hawakubatizwa naye.
sw.B: Lakini Mafarisayo na wataalamu wa sheria walikataa kile ambacho Mungu alikusudia kwa ajili yao, kwa kuwa hawakukubali kubatizwa na Yohana.
sw.R: Lakini Mafarisayo na wataalamu wa sheria ya Mungu walikiacha kile ambacho Mungu alitaka kuwafanyia. Hawakukubali Yohana awabatize.

decisions.choice: experts in the law: men trained in the law of Moses, much like the scribes
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word for the experts who taught and applied God's law (10:25; 11:45-52). Many were Pharisees.

decisions.choice: the purpose of God: God's plan, here his call to repent through John
decisions.reason: The noun means a plan or decision. Luke uses it of God's saving plan (Acts 2:23; 20:27).

decisions.choice: for themselves: the plan was meant for them, and they rejected it
decisions.reason: The phrase can go with "rejected" (they rejected it, to their own loss) or with "purpose" (God's purpose for them). Either way they turned down what God offered them.

decisions.choice: Pharisees: a movement of Jews devoted to keeping God's law in every part of life
decisions.reason: As explained at 5:17 and 6:2.

decisions.choice: experts in God's law (R); experts in the law (L, B)
decisions.reason: Today "lawyer" suggests courts and contracts. The word means someone expert in the law of Moses.

decisions.choice: John
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name John, so the reader does not think of Jesus.

decisions.choice: los expertos en la ley
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording for these men trained in the law of Moses (meaning decision m1), kept apart from "escribas" for the other word; Readable adds "de Dios" as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: wataalamu wa sheria
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording for these men trained in the law of Moses (meaning decision m1), kept apart from "walimu wa sheria", the Readable word for the scribes; Readable adds "ya Mungu" as the English Readable does.

source.text: Τίνι οὖν ὁμοιώσω τοὺς ἀνθρώπους τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης, καὶ τίνι εἰσὶν ὅμοιοι;

records.literal_gloss: To what then will I liken the people of the generation this, and to what are they like?

en.L: "To what then shall I compare the {{gender:people|men}} of this generation, and what are they like?
en.B: Jesus went on, "Then how shall I picture the {{gender:people|men}} of this generation? What are they like?
en.R: Jesus continued, "How can I describe the {{gender:people|men}} who live today? What are they like?

es.L: «¿Con qué, pues, compararé a {{gender:las personas|los hombres}} de esta generación, y a qué se parecen?
es.B: Jesús continuó: «¿Con qué compararé entonces a {{gender:las personas|los hombres}} de esta generación? ¿A qué se parecen?
es.R: Jesús siguió diciendo: «¿Cómo puedo describir a {{gender:las personas|los hombres}} que viven hoy? ¿A qué se parecen?

sw.L: "Basi niwafananishe watu wa kizazi hiki na nini, nao wanafanana na nini?
sw.B: Yesu aliendelea kusema, "Basi niwafananishe watu wa kizazi hiki na nini? Wao ni kama nini?
sw.R: Yesu aliendelea kusema, "Niwaelezeje watu wanaoishi siku hizi? Wao ni kama nini?

decisions.choice: this generation: the people of Jesus's time, as a whole
alternatives: a period of thirty or forty years
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of the people of his day who refused both John and himself (11:29-32; 17:25).

decisions.choice: two questions with one meaning
decisions.reason: The second question repeats the first, a Hebrew way of giving a saying weight.

decisions.choice: people: human beings, men and women
decisions.reason: The word means people in general.

decisions.choice: Jesus went on (B); Jesus continued (R)
decisions.reason: After the narrator's comment in 7:29-30, Balanced and Readable say that Jesus is speaking again. Literal only opens the quotation again.

decisions.choice: who live today
decisions.reason: Readable says what "generation" means here.

decisions.choice: {{gender:las personas|los hombres}}
decisions.reason: Spanish has two wordings here, as English does: "las personas" for men and women (meaning decision m3), "los hombres" as the traditional form. "Las personas" rather than "la gente" keeps the plural verbs ("se parecen", "viven") the same under both settings.

decisions.choice: watu, no gender span
decisions.reason: The English has "people|men". "Watu" already means men and women (meaning decision m3), and "wanaume" would mean males only, so there is nothing for the setting to change.

source.text: ὅμοιοί εἰσιν παιδίοις τοῖς ἐν ἀγορᾷ καθημένοις καὶ προσφωνοῦσιν ἀλλήλοις, ἃ λέγει· Ηὐλήσαμεν ὑμῖν καὶ οὐκ ὠρχήσασθε· ἐθρηνήσαμεν καὶ οὐκ ἐκλαύσατε·

records.literal_gloss: Like they are to children who in marketplace are sitting and calling to one another, which says, We played the flute for you and not you danced; we sang a lament and not you wept.

en.L: They are like children sitting in [the] marketplace and calling to one another, who say, 'We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we sang a lament, and you did not weep.'
en.B: They are like small children who sit in the town square and shout to each other, 'We played wedding music on the flute for you, and you would not dance. We sang a funeral song, and you would not cry.'
en.R: They are like children sitting in the town square. They call out to each other, 'We played happy music on the flute for you, but you would not dance! We sang sad songs, but you would not cry!'

es.L: Se parecen a niños sentados en [la] plaza y que se gritan unos a otros, diciendo: “{{plural_you:Les|Os}} tocamos la flauta, y no {{plural_you:bailaron|bailasteis}}; entonamos lamentos, y no {{plural_you:lloraron|llorasteis}}”.
es.B: Son como niños pequeños que se sientan en la plaza del pueblo y se gritan unos a otros: “{{plural_you:Les|Os}} tocamos música de boda con la flauta, y no {{plural_you:quisieron|quisisteis}} bailar. Cantamos un canto fúnebre, y no {{plural_you:quisieron|quisisteis}} llorar”.
es.R: Son como niños sentados en la plaza del pueblo. Se gritan unos a otros: “¡{{plural_you:Les|Os}} tocamos música alegre con la flauta, pero no {{plural_you:quisieron|quisisteis}} bailar! ¡Cantamos canciones tristes, pero no {{plural_you:quisieron|quisisteis}} llorar!”.

sw.L: Wanafanana na watoto walioketi sokoni na kuitana wao kwa wao, wakisema, 'Tuliwapigia filimbi, nanyi hamkucheza; tuliomboleza, nanyi hamkulia.'
sw.B: Wao ni kama watoto wadogo wanaoketi uwanjani mjini na kuitana wao kwa wao, 'Tuliwapigia filimbi muziki wa harusi, lakini hamkutaka kucheza. Tuliimba wimbo wa maziko, lakini hamkutaka kulia.'
sw.R: Wao ni kama watoto walioketi uwanjani mjini. Wanaitana wao kwa wao, 'Tuliwapigia filimbi muziki wa furaha, lakini hamkutaka kucheza! Tuliimba nyimbo za huzuni, lakini hamkutaka kulia!'

decisions.choice: the marketplace: the open square of a town, where people met and children played
decisions.reason: Every town had an open space for buying, selling and meeting.

decisions.choice: played the flute, sang a lament: children playing at weddings and at funerals
decisions.reason: Flute music went with weddings and feasts; wailing songs went with funerals. The children want the others to play their game, but the others will join in neither. So the people of this generation would accept neither John nor Jesus.

decisions.choice: which says: what the children call out
decisions.reason: The singular "says" goes with the neuter plural "children", as Greek allows.

decisions.choice: wedding music (B), happy music (R); a funeral song (B), sad songs (R)
alternatives: played the flute; sang a lament
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what kind of game the children were playing, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: plural_you spans in the children's words
decisions.reason: The children call to the other children, a plural "you", so their words take the setting like Jesus's own.

source.text: ἐλήλυθεν γὰρ Ἰωάννης ὁ βαπτιστὴς μὴ ἐσθίων ἄρτον μήτε πίνων οἶνον, καὶ λέγετε· Δαιμόνιον ἔχει·

records.literal_gloss: Has come for John the Baptist not eating bread nor drinking wine, and you say, A demon he has;

en.L: For John the Baptist has come not eating bread nor drinking wine, and you say, 'He has a demon.'
en.B: For John the Baptist has come eating no bread and drinking no wine, and you say, 'There is a demon in him.'
en.R: John the Baptist came, and he went without bread and did not drink wine. And you said, 'He has a demon in him!'

es.L: Porque ha venido Juan el Bautista sin comer pan ni beber vino, y {{plural_you:dicen|decís}}: “Tiene un demonio”.
es.B: Porque ha venido Juan el Bautista, que no come pan ni bebe vino, y {{plural_you:ustedes dicen|vosotros decís}}: “Tiene un demonio dentro”.
es.R: Juan el Bautista vino, y no comía pan ni bebía vino. Y {{plural_you:ustedes dijeron|vosotros dijisteis}}: “¡Tiene un demonio dentro!”.

sw.L: Kwa maana Yohana Mbatizaji amekuja bila kula mkate wala kunywa divai, nanyi mnasema, 'Ana pepo.'
sw.B: Kwa maana Yohana Mbatizaji amekuja, hali mkate wala hanywi divai, nanyi mnasema, 'Ana pepo ndani yake.'
sw.R: Yohana Mbatizaji alikuja, naye hakula mkate wala hakunywa divai. Nanyi mkasema, 'Ana pepo ndani yake!'

decisions.choice: not eating bread nor drinking wine: John lived a strict life of fasting
decisions.reason: John was to drink no wine (1:15), and he lived in the wilderness on simple food (Matthew 3:4). His disciples fasted often (5:33).

decisions.choice: he has a demon: he is mad, driven by an evil spirit
decisions.reason: People said the same of Jesus (John 7:20; 10:20). It dismissed John as out of his mind.

decisions.choice: past tense: came, said
decisions.reason: Readable tells it as a story of what happened.

source.text: ἐλήλυθεν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐσθίων καὶ πίνων, καὶ λέγετε· Ἰδοὺ ἄνθρωπος φάγος καὶ οἰνοπότης, φίλος τελωνῶν καὶ ἁμαρτωλῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Has come the Son of the Man eating and drinking, and you say, Look, a man a glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners.

en.L: The Son of Man has come eating and drinking, and you say, 'Look, a man who is a glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!'
en.B: The Son of Man has come eating and drinking, and you say, 'Look at the man! He is greedy for food and a heavy drinker, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!'
en.R: The Son of Man came, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} ate and drank. And you said, 'Look at {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}! He eats too much and drinks too much wine. He is a friend of tax collectors and sinners!'

es.L: Ha venido el Hijo del Hombre comiendo y bebiendo, y {{plural_you:dicen|decís}}: “Ahí está un hombre comilón y borracho, amigo de publicanos y pecadores”.
es.B: Ha venido el Hijo del Hombre, que come y bebe, y {{plural_you:dicen|decís}}: “¡{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}} a ese hombre! Es un glotón y un gran bebedor, amigo de cobradores de impuestos y de pecadores”.
es.R: El Hijo del Hombre vino, y comía y bebía. Y {{plural_you:ustedes dijeron|vosotros dijisteis}}: “¡{{plural_you:Fíjense|Fijaos}} en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}! Come demasiado y bebe demasiado vino. ¡Es amigo de cobradores de impuestos y de pecadores!”.

sw.L: Mwana wa Adamu amekuja akila na kunywa, nanyi mnasema, 'Tazama, mtu mlafi na mlevi, rafiki wa watoza ushuru na wenye dhambi.'
sw.B: Mwana wa Adamu amekuja akila na kunywa, nanyi mnasema, 'Mwangalieni mtu huyu! Ni mlafi na mlevi, rafiki wa watoza ushuru na wenye dhambi!'
sw.R: Mwana wa Adamu alikuja, naye alikula na kunywa. Nanyi mkasema, 'Mwangalieni! Anakula kupita kiasi na kunywa divai kupita kiasi. Ni rafiki wa watoza ushuru na wenye dhambi!'

decisions.choice: a glutton and a drunkard: the charge against a rebellious son in Deuteronomy 21:20
alternatives: a mere insult with no echo
decisions.reason: The law speaks of a stubborn son who is a glutton and a drunkard. The words brand Jesus as a disgrace to his people.

decisions.choice: a friend of tax collectors and sinners: one who shares meals with outcasts
alternatives: one who approves of their sins
decisions.reason: Jesus ate with tax collectors and sinners (5:29-32), and he will do so again (7:36-50; 15:1-2; 19:7).

decisions.choice: the Son of Man: Jesus's name for himself, as in 5:24 and 6:5
decisions.reason: Jesus contrasts John's fasting with his own way of life, which was open to everyone.

decisions.choice: greedy for food and a heavy drinker (B); eats too much and drinks too much wine (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use everyday words for the old ones.

decisions.choice: Look (L); Look at the man (B); Look at him (R)
decisions.reason: Here the word points at Jesus with scorn, so Balanced and Readable keep it and say what is pointed at. "Behold" is old-fashioned.

decisions.choice: el Hijo del Hombre
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording for Jesus's name for himself (meaning decision m3), a title, never under the gender setting.

decisions.choice: Ahí está
decisions.reason: The people say "look" to one another, not to one person; "ahí está" points at him without choosing a singular or plural "you". Balanced and Readable say it to the group, with the plural_you setting.

decisions.choice: Mwana wa Adamu
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording for Jesus's name for himself (meaning decision m3), as in John; never under the gender setting.

decisions.choice: Mwangalieni, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The English Readable "Look at him" takes the setting; Swahili carries "him" in the verb (-m-), which cannot take a capital.

source.text: καὶ ἐδικαιώθη ἡ σοφία ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν τέκνων αὐτῆς.

records.literal_gloss: And was justified the wisdom by all the children of her.

en.L: And wisdom was justified by all her children."
en.B: Yet wisdom is shown to be right by all who are her children."
en.R: But God's wisdom is shown to be right by all the people who accept it."

es.L: Y la sabiduría fue reivindicada por todos sus hijos».
es.B: Pero todos los hijos de la sabiduría demuestran que ella tiene razón».
es.R: Pero todas las personas que aceptan la sabiduría de Dios muestran que esa sabiduría tiene razón».

sw.L: Na hekima ilionyeshwa kuwa sahihi na watoto wake wote."
sw.B: Lakini hekima inaonyeshwa kuwa sahihi na wote walio watoto wake."
sw.R: Lakini watu wote wanaoikubali hekima ya Mungu wanaonyesha kwamba hekima hiyo ni sahihi."

decisions.choice: wisdom: God's wisdom, seen in his plan through John and Jesus
decisions.reason: In Proverbs, wisdom is pictured as a woman who calls people to follow her (Proverbs 8:1-4; 9:1-6). Here she stands for God's wise plan, which sent John and Jesus in different ways (compare 11:49).

decisions.choice: her children: those who accept wisdom and live by it
decisions.reason: In Hebrew speech the children of something share its nature. The children of wisdom are the people who accepted God's call through John and Jesus, like the tax collectors of 7:29.

decisions.choice: was justified: was shown to be right
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in 7:29: the people who accepted John's baptism declared God right. The tense is a timeless past: wisdom has been proved right every time.

decisions.choice: is shown to be right
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the verb means here, and use the present, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: God's wisdom; the people who accept it
decisions.reason: Readable names whose wisdom it is and explains "her children".

decisions.choice: fue reivindicada
decisions.reason: Shown to be in the right (meaning decision m3). "Justificada" in Spanish now usually means excused.

decisions.choice: ilionyeshwa kuwa sahihi (L); inaonyeshwa kuwa sahihi (B); wanaonyesha kwamba ni sahihi (R)
decisions.reason: Shown to be in the right (meaning decision m3). "Kuhesabiwa haki" is the phrase for being made righteous before God, and "haki" is kept for righteousness, so it would point the wrong way here.

source.text: Ἠρώτα δέ τις αὐτὸν τῶν Φαρισαίων ἵνα φάγῃ μετ’ αὐτοῦ· καὶ εἰσελθὼν εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ Φαρισαίου κατεκλίθη.

records.literal_gloss: Was asking then one of him of the Pharisees that he would eat with him; and having entered into the house of the Pharisee he reclined.

en.L: Now one of the Pharisees was asking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to eat with him, and entering into the Pharisee's house, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} reclined [at table].
en.B: One of the Pharisees invited Jesus to a meal with him. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went into the Pharisee's house and took {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} place at the table.
en.R: A Pharisee invited Jesus to come and eat with him. So Jesus went to the Pharisee's house and lay down on a couch at the table, as people did for a dinner.

es.L: Y uno de los fariseos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} rogaba que comiera con él; y entrando en la casa del fariseo, se reclinó [a la mesa].
es.B: Uno de los fariseos invitó a Jesús a comer con él. Entonces Jesús entró en la casa del fariseo y ocupó {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} lugar a la mesa.
es.R: Un fariseo invitó a Jesús a comer con él. Entonces Jesús fue a la casa del fariseo y se recostó junto a la mesa, como se hacía en las cenas.

sw.L: Basi mmoja wa Mafarisayo alikuwa akimwomba ale pamoja naye; kisha akaingia nyumbani mwa yule Farisayo, akaegemea [mezani].
sw.B: Mmoja wa Mafarisayo alimkaribisha Yesu kula chakula pamoja naye. Basi Yesu akaingia nyumbani kwa yule Farisayo, akakaa mahali {{deity_pronoun:pake|Pake}} mezani.
sw.R: Farisayo mmoja alimkaribisha Yesu aje kula pamoja naye. Kwa hiyo Yesu alikwenda nyumbani kwa yule Farisayo, akajilaza kwenye kochi karibu na meza, kama watu walivyofanya wakati wa karamu.

decisions.choice: reclined: lay on a couch at the table, leaning on one elbow
decisions.reason: At a formal meal guests lay on couches around a low table, with their feet away from it. This is why the woman could stand behind Jesus at his feet (7:38).

decisions.choice: a Pharisee's invitation: Jesus ate with Pharisees as well as with sinners
decisions.reason: Luke tells of three meals with Pharisees (7:36; 11:37; 14:1). Jesus has just been called a friend of sinners (7:34).

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus at the start of a new section.

decisions.choice: lay down on a couch at the table, as people did for a dinner
decisions.reason: Readable explains the custom, which the next verses need.

decisions.choice: se reclinó [a la mesa]
decisions.reason: Guests at a dinner lay on couches around the table (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps the reclining, with the table supplied; Readable describes it, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: akaegemea [mezani] (reclined [at table])
decisions.reason: Guests at a dinner lay on couches around the table (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps the reclining, with the table supplied; Readable describes it, as the English Readable does.

source.text: καὶ ἰδοὺ γυνὴ ἥτις ἦν ἐν τῇ πόλει ἁμαρτωλός, καὶ ἐπιγνοῦσα ὅτι κατάκειται ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ τοῦ Φαρισαίου, κομίσασα ἀλάβαστρον μύρου καὶ στᾶσα ὀπίσω παρὰ τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ κλαίουσα, τοῖς δάκρυσιν ἤρξατο βρέχειν τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ καὶ ταῖς θριξὶν τῆς κεφαλῆς αὐτῆς ἐξέμασσεν, καὶ κατεφίλει τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ καὶ ἤλειφεν τῷ μύρῳ.

records.literal_gloss: And look a woman who was in the city a sinner, and having learned that he is reclining in the house of the Pharisee, having brought an alabaster flask of perfume \v 38 and having stood behind at the feet of him weeping, with the tears she began to wet the feet of him and with the hairs of the head of her she was wiping, and was kissing the feet of him and was anointing with the perfume.

en.L: And look, a woman in the town who was a sinner, learning that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was reclining [at table] in the Pharisee's house, brought an alabaster flask of perfume, \v 38 and standing behind at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet, weeping, she began to wet {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet with [her] tears, and she was wiping [them] with the hair of her head, and she was kissing {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet and anointing [them] with the perfume.
en.B: Now there was a woman in the town who was a sinner. When she found out that Jesus was at table in the Pharisee's house, she came with an alabaster flask of perfume. \v 38 She stood behind {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet, crying, and began to wet {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet with her tears. She dried them with the hair of her head, and she kissed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet over and over and anointed them with the perfume.
en.R: In that town there was a woman everyone knew as a sinner. She heard that Jesus was eating at the Pharisee's house. So she came, carrying a beautiful stone jar full of expensive perfume. \v 38 She stood behind Jesus at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet, and she was crying. Her tears fell on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet and made them wet. Then she dried {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet with her hair. She kept kissing them and pouring the perfume on them.

es.L: Y mira, una mujer que en la ciudad era pecadora, al saber que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} estaba reclinado [a la mesa] en la casa del fariseo, trajo un frasco de alabastro con perfume, \v 38 y poniéndose detrás, junto a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} pies, llorando, comenzó a mojar {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} pies con [sus] lágrimas, y [los] secaba con los cabellos de su cabeza, y besaba {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} pies y [los] ungía con el perfume.
es.B: Había en el pueblo una mujer que era pecadora. Cuando supo que Jesús estaba a la mesa en la casa del fariseo, llegó con un frasco de alabastro lleno de perfume. \v 38 Se puso detrás de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} pies, llorando, y comenzó a mojar {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} pies con sus lágrimas. Los secaba con los cabellos de su cabeza, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} besaba los pies una y otra vez y los ungía con el perfume.
es.R: En aquel pueblo había una mujer a la que todos conocían como pecadora. Ella oyó que Jesús estaba comiendo en la casa del fariseo. Así que fue allá con un hermoso frasco de piedra lleno de un perfume caro. \v 38 Se puso detrás de Jesús, junto a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} pies, y lloraba. Las lágrimas de ella caían sobre {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} pies y los mojaban. Después {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} secó los pies con su cabello. No dejaba de besarlos y de derramar el perfume sobre ellos.

sw.L: Na tazama, mwanamke mmoja aliyekuwa mwenye dhambi katika mji ule, alipojua kwamba anaegemea [mezani] nyumbani mwa yule Farisayo, alileta chupa ya alabasta yenye manukato, \v 38 akasimama nyuma karibu na miguu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} akilia, akaanza kuilowesha miguu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kwa machozi, akawa akiipangusa kwa nywele za kichwa chake, akiibusu miguu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} na kuipaka manukato.
sw.B: Basi kulikuwa na mwanamke mmoja katika mji ule ambaye alikuwa mwenye dhambi. Alipojua kwamba Yesu alikuwa mezani nyumbani mwa yule Farisayo, alikuja na chupa ya alabasta yenye manukato. \v 38 Akasimama nyuma {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, karibu na miguu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, akilia, akaanza kuilowesha miguu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kwa machozi yake. Akaipangusa kwa nywele za kichwa chake, akaibusu miguu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} tena na tena, akaipaka manukato.
sw.R: Katika mji ule kulikuwa na mwanamke ambaye kila mtu alimjua kuwa mwenye dhambi. Alisikia kwamba Yesu alikuwa akila nyumbani kwa yule Farisayo. Kwa hiyo akaja, amebeba chupa nzuri ya jiwe iliyojaa manukato ya bei ghali. \v 38 Akasimama nyuma ya Yesu karibu na miguu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, naye alikuwa akilia. Machozi yake yakadondoka juu ya miguu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} na kuilowesha. Kisha akaipangusa miguu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kwa nywele zake. Akaendelea kuibusu na kuimwagia manukato.

decisions.choice: a sinner: a woman known in the town for an immoral life
alternatives: a woman who had committed some private sin
decisions.reason: The word marks someone whose way of life openly broke God's law (5:30). Luke does not say what her sin was. Later tradition made her Mary Magdalene, but Luke introduces Mary Magdalene in the next chapter as a different person (8:2).

decisions.choice: an alabaster flask of perfume: a sealed jar of soft stone holding costly perfumed oil
decisions.reason: Alabaster was a smooth, pale stone used for jars of precious perfume. The perfume was far more costly than the olive oil of 7:46.

decisions.choice: wiping his feet with her hair: an act of humble devotion, unusual in public
decisions.reason: A respectable woman did not let down her hair in front of men. She uses her own hair and tears where the host had given no water (7:44).

decisions.choice: this is not the anointing at Bethany
alternatives: the same event as Mark 14:3-9 and John 12:1-8
decisions.reason: Those Gospels tell of a woman who anointed Jesus at Bethany, near Jerusalem, in the last week of his life. Luke's story takes place in Galilee, in a Pharisee's house, much earlier. Luke does not tell the Bethany anointing.

decisions.choice: began to wet, was kissing, was anointing: actions continued over time
decisions.reason: The tenses describe what she kept on doing. Jesus says she has not stopped kissing his feet (7:45).

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word to draw attention to what follows. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence, as in Matthew 1:20.

decisions.choice: a beautiful stone jar
decisions.reason: Readable describes alabaster instead of naming it.

decisions.choice: anointed (B); pouring the perfume on (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what anointing the feet meant.

source.text: ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ Φαρισαῖος ὁ καλέσας αὐτὸν εἶπεν ἐν ἑαυτῷ λέγων· Οὗτος εἰ ἦν προφήτης, ἐγίνωσκεν ἂν τίς καὶ ποταπὴ ἡ γυνὴ ἥτις ἅπτεται αὐτοῦ, ὅτι ἁμαρτωλός ἐστιν.

records.literal_gloss: Having seen then the Pharisee the [one] having invited him spoke within himself saying, This [man] if he were a prophet, would know who and what kind the woman who is touching him, that a sinner she is.

en.L: Now when the Pharisee who had invited {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} saw [this], he spoke within himself, saying, "This man, if {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} were a prophet, would know who and what sort of woman [this is] who is touching {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, that she is a sinner."
en.B: The Pharisee who had invited {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} saw this and said to himself, "This man, if {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} were a prophet, would have known who this woman is who is touching {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and what sort of woman she is: a sinner."
en.R: The Pharisee who had invited Jesus saw what was happening. He thought, "This man cannot be a prophet. A prophet would know who this woman is, the one touching {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He would know what kind of woman she is. She is a sinner!"

es.L: Y al ver [esto] el fariseo que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} había invitado, dijo dentro de sí: «Este, si fuera profeta, sabría quién y qué clase de mujer [es] la que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} está tocando, que es una pecadora».
es.B: El fariseo que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} había invitado vio esto y se dijo: «Si este hombre fuera profeta, sabría quién es esta mujer que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} toca, y qué clase de mujer es: una pecadora».
es.R: El fariseo que había invitado a Jesús vio lo que pasaba. Pensó: «Este hombre no puede ser profeta. Un profeta sabría quién es esta mujer que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} está tocando. Sabría qué clase de mujer es. ¡Es una pecadora!».

sw.L: Basi yule Farisayo aliyemwalika alipoona [hayo], alinena ndani yake, akisema, "Huyu, kama angekuwa nabii, angejua ni nani, na ni mwanamke wa namna gani huyu anayemgusa, kwamba ni mwenye dhambi."
sw.B: Yule Farisayo aliyemwalika alipoona hayo, alisema moyoni, "Kama mtu huyu angekuwa nabii, angejua mwanamke huyu anayemgusa ni nani, na ni wa namna gani: ni mwenye dhambi."
sw.R: Yule Farisayo aliyemwalika Yesu aliona yaliyokuwa yakitokea. Akawaza, "Mtu huyu hawezi kuwa nabii. Nabii angejua mwanamke huyu anayemgusa ni nani. Angejua ni mwanamke wa namna gani. Ni mwenye dhambi!"

decisions.choice: if he were a prophet, he would know: the Pharisee assumes that Jesus is not a prophet
alternatives: a real question whether he is
decisions.reason: The form of the sentence states something contrary to fact: he would know, but he does not, so he is no prophet. Jesus answers by reading the Pharisee's own unspoken thoughts (7:40).

decisions.choice: a prophet, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the prophet, the reading of some early manuscripts
decisions.reason: A few early manuscripts have "the prophet", meaning the prophet like Moses promised in Deuteronomy 18:15. Most have "a prophet". Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: touching: the touch of a sinner would make him unclean, in the Pharisee's eyes
decisions.reason: The Pharisees took great care to avoid what made them unclean. The host thinks Jesus should have known and drawn back.

decisions.choice: spoke within himself: thought to himself, without speaking aloud
decisions.reason: The phrase means private thought (3:8; 12:17).

decisions.choice: This man cannot be a prophet. A prophet would know
alternatives: if he were a prophet, he would know
decisions.reason: Readable states the conclusion the condition implies, as the meaning decision explains, and then gives the reasoning.

source.text: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν· Σίμων, ἔχω σοί τι εἰπεῖν.

records.literal_gloss: And answering Jesus said to him, Simon, I have to you something to say.

en.L: And answering, Jesus said to him, "Simon, I have something to say to you."
en.B: Jesus answered him, "Simon, there is something I want to tell you."
en.R: Jesus answered the Pharisee's thoughts. He said, "Simon, I have something to tell you."

es.L: Y respondiendo, Jesús le dijo: «Simón, tengo algo que decirte».
es.B: Jesús le respondió: «Simón, hay algo que quiero decirte».
es.R: Jesús respondió a lo que el fariseo estaba pensando. Le dijo: «Simón, tengo algo que decirte».

sw.L: Naye Yesu akajibu, akamwambia, "Simoni, nina neno la kukuambia."
sw.B: Yesu alimjibu, "Simoni, kuna jambo nataka kukuambia."
sw.R: Yesu aliyajibu mawazo ya yule Farisayo. Akasema, "Simoni, nina jambo la kukuambia."

decisions.choice: answering: Jesus answers what the Pharisee only thought
decisions.reason: The host spoke only within himself (7:39). Jesus answers him, which shows that he is indeed a prophet who knows hearts (5:22; 6:8).

decisions.choice: Simon: the Pharisee's name
decisions.reason: Simon was a common name. This Simon is the Pharisee who invited Jesus, not the disciple Simon Peter.

decisions.choice: answered the Pharisee's thoughts
decisions.reason: Readable says what Jesus answered, as the meaning decision explains.

source.text: ὁ δέ· Διδάσκαλε, εἰπέ, φησίν.

records.literal_gloss: And he: Teacher, say [it], he says.

en.L: And he says, "Teacher, say [it]."
en.B: "Say it, Teacher," he replied.
en.R: Simon said, "Tell me, Teacher."

es.L: Y él dice: «Maestro, dilo».
es.B: «Dilo, Maestro», respondió él.
es.R: Simón dijo: «Dime, Maestro».

sw.L: Naye anasema, "Mwalimu, sema."
sw.B: Akajibu, "Sema, Mwalimu."
sw.R: Simoni akasema, "Niambie, Mwalimu."

decisions.choice: Teacher: a respectful title for a teacher of the law
decisions.reason: Simon gives Jesus the title of a respected teacher (3:12), not more.

decisions.choice: he says: a present tense in the story
decisions.reason: Greek often tells a past event in the present for vividness.

decisions.choice: replied (B); said (R)
decisions.reason: English tells the story in the past.

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal (dice); past at Balanced and Readable (respondió, dijo)
decisions.reason: Luke tells this past event in the present (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the past, as Spanish narrative does.

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal (anasema); past at Balanced and Readable (akajibu, akasema)
decisions.reason: Luke tells this past event in the present (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the narrative past.

source.text: δύο χρεοφειλέται ἦσαν δανιστῇ τινι· ὁ εἷς ὤφειλεν δηνάρια πεντακόσια, ὁ δὲ ἕτερος πεντήκοντα.

records.literal_gloss: Two debtors were to a moneylender certain; the one owed denarii five hundred, the and other fifty.

en.L: "Two debtors belonged to a certain moneylender; the one owed 500 denarii, and the other fifty.
en.B: Jesus said, "A moneylender had two men who owed him money. One owed him 500 denarii, and the other fifty.
en.R: Jesus said, "Two men owed money to a man who lent money. One of them owed him 500 silver coins. The other owed him fifty.

es.L: «Dos deudores tenía cierto prestamista; uno le debía quinientos denarios, y el otro cincuenta.
es.B: Jesús dijo: «Un prestamista tenía dos hombres que le debían dinero. Uno le debía quinientos denarios, y el otro cincuenta.
es.R: Jesús dijo: «Dos hombres le debían dinero a un hombre que prestaba dinero. Uno de ellos le debía quinientas monedas de plata. El otro le debía cincuenta.

sw.L: "Wadeni wawili walikuwa na mkopeshaji fulani; mmoja alidaiwa dinari mia tano, na yule mwingine hamsini.
sw.B: Yesu alisema, "Mkopeshaji mmoja alikuwa na watu wawili waliokuwa na deni lake. Mmoja alikuwa anadaiwa dinari mia tano, na mwingine hamsini.
sw.R: Yesu alisema, "Watu wawili walikuwa wanadaiwa fedha na mtu mmoja aliyekopesha fedha. Mmoja wao alidaiwa sarafu mia tano za fedha. Yule mwingine alidaiwa hamsini.

decisions.choice: denarii: Roman silver coins, each the usual pay for a day's work
decisions.reason: A denarius was a laborer's wage for a day (Matthew 20:2). So 500 denarii was more than a year's wages, and fifty about two months' wages. Both were real debts; one was ten times the other.

decisions.choice: a story told to answer Simon's thoughts
decisions.reason: Jesus answers the unspoken charge of 7:39 with a short parable.

decisions.choice: Jesus said
decisions.reason: The Greek starts the story without a new speech verb. Balanced and Readable name the speaker after Simon's reply; Literal only opens the quotation.

decisions.choice: silver coins (R); denarii (L, B)
decisions.reason: Readable describes the coin instead of naming it. A modern sum would be misleading, since wages differ from place to place; the meaning decision gives the coin's worth.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and closes at the end of 7:42
decisions.reason: The parable and its question are one speech.

decisions.choice: denarios (L, B); monedas de plata (R), with no units span
alternatives: a units span giving the sums in wages
decisions.reason: The English names the coin here (meaning decision m1) and has no units span, so Spanish has none either; Readable says "monedas de plata" as the English Readable says "silver coins".

decisions.choice: dinari (L, B); sarafu za fedha (R), with no units span
alternatives: a units span giving the sums in wages
decisions.reason: The English names the coin here (meaning decision m1) and has no units span, so Swahili has none either; Readable says "sarafu za fedha" as the English Readable says "silver coins".

source.text: μὴ ἐχόντων αὐτῶν ἀποδοῦναι ἀμφοτέροις ἐχαρίσατο.

records.literal_gloss: Not having they to repay, both he forgave.

en.L: When they did not have [the means] to repay, he freely forgave [them] both.
en.B: Neither of them could pay him back, so he freely canceled the debts of both.
en.R: Neither of them had the money to pay him back. So he kindly canceled what both of them owed.

es.L: Como no tenían [con qué] pagar, les perdonó [la deuda] a ambos.
es.B: Ninguno de los dos podía pagarle, así que él les perdonó generosamente la deuda a ambos.
es.R: Ninguno de los dos tenía dinero para pagarle. Así que él, con bondad, les perdonó a los dos lo que le debían.

sw.L: Walipokuwa hawana [cha] kulipa, aliwasamehe wote wawili bure.
sw.B: Hakuna hata mmoja wao aliyeweza kumlipa, kwa hiyo aliwafutia wote wawili madeni yao bila malipo.
sw.R: Hakuna kati yao aliyekuwa na fedha za kumlipa. Kwa hiyo kwa wema wake aliwafutia wote wawili madeni yao.

decisions.choice: forgave: canceled the debt as a free gift
decisions.reason: The verb means to give freely, as a favor (7:21). The debts are wiped out, not put off. The word prepares for the forgiveness of sins in 7:47-48.

decisions.choice: the debts of both (B); what both of them owed (R)
decisions.reason: English needs to say what was forgiven.

source.text: τίς οὖν αὐτῶν πλεῖον ἀγαπήσει αὐτόν;

records.literal_gloss: Which then of them more will love him?

en.L: Which of them, then, will love him more?"
en.B: So which of the two will love him more?"
en.R: Which of these two men will love the moneylender more?"

es.L: ¿Cuál de ellos, pues, lo amará más?».
es.B: ¿Cuál de los dos lo amará más?».
es.R: ¿Cuál de estos dos hombres amará más al prestamista?».

sw.L: Basi ni yupi kati yao atakayempenda zaidi?"
sw.B: Basi ni yupi kati ya hao wawili atakayempenda zaidi?"
sw.R: Ni yupi kati ya watu hao wawili atakayempenda zaidi yule aliyewakopesha?"

decisions.choice: love: grateful love toward the one who forgave
decisions.reason: In the story, love is the response of the one forgiven. The point is applied in 7:47.

decisions.choice: the moneylender
decisions.reason: Readable names the person, so that "him" is clear.

source.text: ἀποκριθεὶς Σίμων εἶπεν· Ὑπολαμβάνω ὅτι ᾧ τὸ πλεῖον ἐχαρίσατο.

records.literal_gloss: Answering Simon said, I suppose that [the one] to whom the more he forgave.

en.L: Simon answered and said, "I suppose [the one] to whom he forgave the more."
en.B: Simon answered, "I would think the one whose larger debt he canceled."
en.R: Simon answered, "I think it is the man who owed more and was forgiven more."

es.L: Respondiendo Simón, dijo: «Supongo que aquel a quien perdonó más».
es.B: Simón respondió: «Me imagino que aquel a quien le perdonó la deuda más grande».
es.R: Simón respondió: «Creo que el que debía más y recibió más perdón».

sw.L: Simoni akajibu, akasema, "Nadhani ni yule aliyesamehewa zaidi."
sw.B: Simoni alijibu, "Nadhani ni yule aliyefutiwa deni kubwa zaidi."
sw.R: Simoni akajibu, "Nafikiri ni yule aliyekuwa anadaiwa zaidi, akasamehewa zaidi."

decisions.choice: I suppose: I take it, a cautious answer
decisions.reason: Simon gives the obvious answer, perhaps reluctantly, sensing where the story is going.

decisions.choice: larger debt (B); owed more (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "the more" refers to.

source.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ὀρθῶς ἔκρινας.

records.literal_gloss: And he said to him, Rightly you have judged.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to him, "You have judged rightly."
en.B: Jesus said to him, "Your judgment is right."
en.R: Jesus said, "You are right."

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} le dijo: «Has juzgado correctamente».
es.B: Jesús le dijo: «Tu juicio es correcto».
es.R: Jesús le dijo: «Tienes razón».

sw.L: Naye akamwambia, "Umehukumu sawasawa."
sw.B: Yesu alimwambia, "Umeamua sawa."
sw.R: Yesu akasema, "Uko sahihi."

decisions.choice: you have judged: you have given a right verdict
decisions.reason: The verb means to decide or give a verdict. Simon has judged rightly in the story, and now must apply it to himself.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker.

source.text: καὶ στραφεὶς πρὸς τὴν γυναῖκα τῷ Σίμωνι ἔφη· Βλέπεις ταύτην τὴν γυναῖκα;

records.literal_gloss: And having turned toward the woman to Simon he said, You see this the woman?

en.L: And turning toward the woman, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to Simon, "Do you see this woman?
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} turned toward the woman and said to Simon, "Do you see this woman?
en.R: Then Jesus turned toward the woman. But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke to Simon: "Do you see this woman?

es.L: Y volviéndose hacia la mujer, dijo a Simón: «¿Ves a esta mujer?
es.B: Entonces se volvió hacia la mujer y le dijo a Simón: «¿Ves a esta mujer?
es.R: Entonces Jesús se volvió hacia la mujer, pero le habló a Simón: «¿Ves a esta mujer?

sw.L: Naye akimgeukia yule mwanamke, akamwambia Simoni, "Unamwona mwanamke huyu?
sw.B: Kisha akamgeukia yule mwanamke, akamwambia Simoni, "Je, unamwona mwanamke huyu?
sw.R: Kisha Yesu akamgeukia yule mwanamke. Lakini alisema na Simoni, "Je, unamwona mwanamke huyu?

decisions.choice: turning to the woman, he spoke to Simon: Jesus looks at her while he speaks to him
decisions.reason: Jesus turns Simon's eyes to the woman he has judged.

decisions.choice: do you see this woman: do you see her as she really is
decisions.reason: Simon has seen only a sinner (7:39). Jesus asks him to look again.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and closes at the end of 7:47
decisions.reason: Jesus's words to Simon run on through 7:47.

source.text: εἰσῆλθόν σου εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν, ὕδωρ μοι ἐπὶ πόδας οὐκ ἔδωκας· αὕτη δὲ τοῖς δάκρυσιν ἔβρεξέν μου τοὺς πόδας καὶ ταῖς θριξὶν αὐτῆς ἐξέμαξεν.

records.literal_gloss: I entered of you into the house, water to me for feet not you gave; she but with the tears wet of me the feet and with the hairs of her wiped [them].

en.L: I entered into your house; you did not give {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} water for [{{deity_pronoun:my|My}}] feet, but she has wet {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} feet with [her] tears and wiped [them] with her hair.
en.B: When I came into your house, you gave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} no water to wash {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} feet. But she has made {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} feet wet with her tears and dried them with her hair.
en.R: I came into your house, and you did not even give {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} water to wash {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} feet. But this woman has washed {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} feet with her tears and dried them with her hair.

es.L: Entré en tu casa; no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} diste agua para [los] pies, pero ella ha mojado {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} pies con [sus] lágrimas y [los] ha secado con sus cabellos.
es.B: Cuando entré en tu casa, no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} diste agua para lavarme los pies. Pero ella {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ha mojado los pies con sus lágrimas y {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} los ha secado con sus cabellos.
es.R: Entré en tu casa, y tú ni siquiera {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} diste agua para lavarme los pies. Pero esta mujer {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ha lavado los pies con sus lágrimas y {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} los ha secado con sus cabellos.

sw.L: Niliingia nyumbani mwako; hukunipa maji kwa ajili ya miguu [{{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}], lakini huyu ameilowesha miguu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} kwa machozi [yake] na kuipangusa kwa nywele zake.
sw.B: Nilipoingia nyumbani mwako, hukunipa maji ya kunawa miguu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. Lakini yeye ameilowesha miguu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} kwa machozi yake na kuipangusa kwa nywele zake.
sw.R: Nilikuja nyumbani kwako, nawe hukunipa hata maji ya kunawa miguu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. Lakini mwanamke huyu ameiosha miguu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} kwa machozi yake, na kuipangusa kwa nywele zake.

decisions.choice: water for my feet: a common courtesy to a guest who had walked on dusty roads
alternatives: a legal duty of the host
decisions.reason: Hosts offered guests water to wash their feet (Genesis 18:4; 24:32; Judges 19:21). Simon did not; Luke does not say whether he meant to insult Jesus.

decisions.choice: she: set in sharp contrast with Simon
decisions.reason: In 7:44-46 each thing Simon did not do is set against what the woman did, in three pairs.

decisions.choice: to wash my feet
decisions.reason: English says what the water was for.

decisions.choice: washed
decisions.reason: Readable carries the contrast with the water Simon did not give.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} on the separate pronoun where English has "my feet"
decisions.reason: Spanish says "me ha mojado los pies" where English says "my feet"; the pronoun for Jesus moves to "me", which takes the setting. Joined forms ("lavarme") take none. The same in verses 45-46.

source.text: φίλημά μοι οὐκ ἔδωκας· αὕτη δὲ ἀφ’ ἧς εἰσῆλθον οὐ διέλιπεν καταφιλοῦσά μου τοὺς πόδας.

records.literal_gloss: A kiss to me not you gave; she but from which I came in not has stopped kissing of me the feet.

en.L: You did not give {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a kiss; but she, from the time I came in, has not stopped kissing {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} feet.
en.B: You did not welcome {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with a kiss. But ever since I came in, she has kept on kissing {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} feet.
en.R: You did not greet {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with a kiss. But from the time I came in, she has not stopped kissing {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} feet.

es.L: No {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} diste un beso; pero ella, desde que entré, no ha dejado de besar {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} pies.
es.B: No {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} recibiste con un beso. Pero ella, desde que entré, no ha dejado de besarme los pies.
es.R: Tú no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} saludaste con un beso. Pero ella, desde que entré, no ha dejado de besarme los pies.

sw.L: Hukunipa busu; lakini huyu, tangu nilipoingia, hajaacha kuibusu miguu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}.
sw.B: Hukunikaribisha kwa busu. Lakini tangu nilipoingia, yeye hajaacha kuibusu miguu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}.
sw.R: Hukunisalimu kwa busu. Lakini tangu nilipoingia, mwanamke huyu hajaacha kuibusu miguu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}.

decisions.choice: a kiss: the usual greeting of welcome
decisions.reason: A host greeted an honored guest with a kiss on the cheek (15:20; 22:47-48).

decisions.choice: I came in, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: she came in, the reading of some manuscripts
decisions.reason: A few manuscripts read "she came in". The SBLGNT reading means she has been kissing his feet as long as he has been there. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

source.text: ἐλαίῳ τὴν κεφαλήν μου οὐκ ἤλειψας· αὕτη δὲ μύρῳ ἤλειψεν τοὺς πόδας μου.

records.literal_gloss: With oil the head of me not you anointed; she but with perfume anointed the feet of me.

en.L: You did not anoint {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} head with oil; but she has anointed {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} feet with perfume.
en.B: You did not anoint {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} head with olive oil, but she has anointed {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} feet with costly perfume.
en.R: You did not put any olive oil on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} head. But she has rubbed expensive perfume on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} feet.

es.L: No ungiste {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} cabeza con aceite; pero ella ha ungido {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} pies con perfume.
es.B: No ungiste {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} cabeza con aceite de oliva, pero ella ha ungido {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} pies con un perfume costoso.
es.R: Tú no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} pusiste nada de aceite de oliva en la cabeza. Pero ella {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ha untado perfume caro en los pies.

sw.L: Hukukipaka kichwa {{deity_pronoun:changu|Changu}} mafuta; lakini huyu ameipaka miguu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} manukato.
sw.B: Hukukipaka kichwa {{deity_pronoun:changu|Changu}} mafuta ya zeituni, lakini yeye ameipaka miguu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} manukato ya thamani.
sw.R: Hukunipaka hata mafuta ya zeituni kichwani. Lakini yeye ameipaka miguu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} manukato ya bei ghali.

decisions.choice: anointing the head with oil: a sign of welcome and honor to a guest
decisions.reason: Olive oil on the head refreshed a guest and honored him (Psalm 23:5; 141:5).

decisions.choice: oil and perfume: common olive oil set against costly perfume
alternatives: two words for the same oil
decisions.reason: Simon did not give even ordinary oil for the head; she gave precious perfume, and for the feet.

decisions.choice: olive oil; costly (B) or expensive (R) perfume
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the contrast between the two oils plain.

source.text: οὗ χάριν, λέγω σοι, ἀφέωνται αἱ ἁμαρτίαι αὐτῆς αἱ πολλαί, ὅτι ἠγάπησεν πολύ· ᾧ δὲ ὀλίγον ἀφίεται, ὀλίγον ἀγαπᾷ.

records.literal_gloss: Of which for the sake, I say to you, have been forgiven the sins of her the many, because she loved much; to whom but little is forgiven, little he loves.

en.L: Therefore, I tell you, her sins, which are many, have been forgiven, for she loved much; but the one to whom little is forgiven loves little."
en.B: So I tell you, her sins, many as they are, stand forgiven; that is why she has shown so much love. But someone who is forgiven little loves little."
en.R: So I tell you, her many sins are forgiven, and that is why she has shown so much love. But a person who has been forgiven only a little loves only a little."

es.L: Por lo cual te digo que sus pecados, que son muchos, han sido perdonados, porque amó mucho; pero aquel a quien poco se le perdona, poco ama».
es.B: Así que te digo que sus pecados, que son muchos, quedan perdonados; por eso ha mostrado tanto amor. Pero aquel a quien se le perdona poco, ama poco».
es.R: Así que te digo que sus muchos pecados están perdonados, y por eso ha mostrado tanto amor. Pero la persona a quien se le ha perdonado solo un poco, ama solo un poco».

sw.L: Kwa sababu hiyo, nakuambia, dhambi zake, zilizo nyingi, zimesamehewa, kwa maana alipenda sana; lakini yeye anayesamehewa kidogo, hupenda kidogo."
sw.B: Kwa hiyo nakuambia, dhambi zake, ingawa ni nyingi, zimesamehewa; ndiyo maana ameonyesha upendo mwingi namna hii. Lakini mtu anayesamehewa kidogo hupenda kidogo."
sw.R: Kwa hiyo nakuambia, dhambi zake nyingi zimesamehewa, na ndiyo sababu ameonyesha upendo mwingi hivi. Lakini mtu aliyesamehewa kidogo tu, hupenda kidogo tu."

decisions.choice: for she loved much: her love shows that she has been forgiven; it is not the price of her forgiveness
alternatives: she is forgiven because she loved much
decisions.reason: The word "for" can give the reason for a fact or the reason we know it. The parable (7:41-43) makes love the result of forgiveness, and the end of the verse says the same: the one forgiven little loves little. In 7:50 Jesus says it was her faith that saved her. Her love is the evidence of a forgiveness she had already received.

decisions.choice: have been forgiven: forgiven, and that stands; God is the one who forgives
alternatives: forgiven at this moment for the first time
decisions.reason: The perfect tense describes a forgiveness that holds, as in 5:20.

decisions.choice: the one forgiven little: a general saying aimed at Simon
alternatives: a statement that Simon has few sins
decisions.reason: Jesus does not say Simon has little to be forgiven. He leaves Simon to see himself in the debtor who loves little.

decisions.choice: that is why she has shown so much love
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say how her love relates to her forgiveness, as the meaning decision explains. A reader could take "because she loved much" to mean she earned it.

source.text: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῇ· Ἀφέωνταί σου αἱ ἁμαρτίαι.

records.literal_gloss: He said then to her, Have been forgiven of you the sins.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to her, "Your sins have been forgiven."
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to her, "Your sins stand forgiven."
en.R: Then Jesus said to the woman, "God has forgiven your sins."

es.L: Y le dijo: «Tus pecados han sido perdonados».
es.B: Entonces le dijo: «Tus pecados quedan perdonados».
es.R: Luego Jesús le dijo a la mujer: «Dios ha perdonado tus pecados».

sw.L: Naye akamwambia, "Dhambi zako zimesamehewa."
sw.B: Kisha akamwambia, "Dhambi zako zimekwisha kusamehewa."
sw.R: Kisha Yesu akamwambia yule mwanamke, "Mungu amekusamehe dhambi zako."

decisions.choice: have been forgiven: as in 5:20, a forgiveness that stands, given by God
alternatives: Jesus forgives her now for the first time
decisions.reason: Jesus declares to her what he has just said about her (7:47). The passive leaves God as the one who forgives, which is why the guests ask who Jesus is (7:49).

decisions.choice: God has forgiven
decisions.reason: Readable names God, as in 5:20.

source.text: καὶ ἤρξαντο οἱ συνανακείμενοι λέγειν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς· Τίς οὗτός ἐστιν ὃς καὶ ἁμαρτίας ἀφίησιν;

records.literal_gloss: And began those reclining with [him] to say within themselves, Who this is who even sins forgives?

en.L: And those reclining [at table] with [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] began to say among themselves, "Who is this, who even forgives sins?"
en.B: The others at the table with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} began to say to one another, "Who is this man, that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} even forgives sins?"
en.R: The other guests began to ask each other, "Who is this man? He even forgives sins!"

es.L: Y los que estaban reclinados [a la mesa] con [{{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}] comenzaron a decir entre sí: «¿Quién es este, que incluso perdona pecados?».
es.B: Los demás que estaban a la mesa con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} comenzaron a decirse unos a otros: «¿Quién es este hombre, que hasta perdona pecados?».
es.R: Los otros invitados comenzaron a preguntarse unos a otros: «¿Quién es este hombre? ¡Hasta perdona pecados!».

sw.L: Na wale walioegemea [mezani] pamoja [{{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}] wakaanza kusema ndani yao, "Huyu ni nani, ambaye hata anasamehe dhambi?"
sw.B: Wale wengine waliokuwa mezani pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} walianza kuambiana, "Mtu huyu ni nani, hata anasamehe dhambi?"
sw.R: Wageni wengine walianza kuulizana, "Mtu huyu ni nani? Hata anasamehe dhambi!"

decisions.choice: among themselves: to one another, or in their own minds
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean either, as in 7:39. Either way they do not ask Jesus.

decisions.choice: who is this: the guests see that he claims to do what only God does
decisions.reason: Only God forgives sins, as the scribes said in 5:21. The question who Jesus is runs through these chapters (5:21; 7:16, 19-20; 9:9, 18-20).

source.text: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς τὴν γυναῖκα· Ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε· πορεύου εἰς εἰρήνην.

records.literal_gloss: He said then to the woman, The faith of you has saved you; go into peace.

en.L: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to the woman, "Your faith has saved you; go in peace."
en.B: But Jesus said to the woman, "Your faith has saved you. Go in peace."
en.R: Jesus said to the woman, "Your faith has saved you. Go home now, and have peace."

es.L: Pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} dijo a la mujer: «Tu fe te ha salvado; vete en paz».
es.B: Pero Jesús le dijo a la mujer: «Tu fe te ha salvado. Vete en paz».
es.R: Jesús le dijo a la mujer: «Tu fe te ha salvado. Vete ahora a tu casa, y que tengas paz».

sw.L: Lakini akamwambia yule mwanamke, "Imani yako imekuokoa; nenda kwa amani."
sw.B: Lakini Yesu alimwambia yule mwanamke, "Imani yako imekuokoa. Nenda kwa amani."
sw.R: Yesu alimwambia yule mwanamke, "Imani yako imekuokoa. Sasa nenda nyumbani, ukawe na amani."

decisions.choice: faith: her trust in Jesus, shown in what she did
decisions.reason: Her tears and her coming to Jesus showed that she trusted him to receive her. Jesus says it was faith, not her love, that saved her (compare 7:47).

decisions.choice: has saved: rescued from sin and its judgment, and restored to God
decisions.reason: The same words are said to people Jesus heals (8:48; 17:19; 18:42). Here no sickness is mentioned: the salvation is the forgiveness of her sins (1:77).

decisions.choice: go in peace: a farewell blessing, here with its full meaning of peace with God
decisions.reason: The words were a usual farewell (1 Samuel 1:17). For the woman they mean she leaves forgiven and whole (8:48).

decisions.choice: Go home now, and have peace
decisions.reason: Readable makes the farewell plain and keeps the key word peace.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker.
